reviews.title: A recording-chain peak is not a material identity
reviews.question: Can a known-input complex ratio recover the total transfer while leaving its physical factorization ambiguous?
reviews.finding: The noiseless known-FIR ratio recovers total transfer and predicts a held-out probe; exact alternative device/echo factorizations remain indistinguishable.
reviews.scope: y=d*e*x; d=[0.7,0.2,0.1]; e=delta[n]+0.6 delta[n-40]; * means linear convolution
withheld: Physical echo or material identification from total transfer
Pressure calibration
Empirical apparatus or biological effect
reviews.incomingEvidence: N5 distinguished actual WAV arithmetic and nonlinear observation operators. P2 identified physical factorization ambiguity and invalid single-record coherence language.
reviews.nextDecision: S1B: test reference cancellation under near-null sensitivity, bounded noise and path drift.

independentChecks.factorization_proof: Associativity: x*(d*e)=(x*d)*e=x*(d_alt*delta). This proves output equivalence for every finite x.

reviews.title: Reference cancellation needs a stable, sensitive chain
reviews.question: How do a near-notch and one-sample path change break reference division?
reviews.finding: Reference cancellation in the declared stable fixture is exact; a one-sample path change mimics an object change, while regularization bounds noise at the cost of calculable bias.
withheld: A universal physical stability or sensitivity threshold
A recovered material transfer in an uncontrolled room
Regularization as removal of uncertainty
reviews.incomingEvidence: S1A total-transfer recovery did not identify factorization; practical comparison requires shared stable chain and nonzero sensitivity.
reviews.nextDecision: S2A: investigate gain-independent single-mode decay from generated PCM and provide recorded-file intake.

independentChecks.proof: (a-sqrt(lambda))^2>=0 implies a/(a^2+lambda)<=1/(2sqrt(lambda)); error separates exact bias and bounded-noise term.

reviews.title: Fit decay from a file, independently of strike gain
reviews.question: Can one shared recording importer recover a declared single-mode decay from quantized WAV at different gains and phases?
reviews.finding: One shared WAV importer/local fitter recovers the declared 500 Hz, 4 s^-1 decay across generated PCM gain/phase cases; silent and clipped files are rejected.
reviews.scope: y(t)=g exp(-alpha t) cos(2pi f t+phase); fit exp(-alpha t)[A cos(2pi ft)+B sin(2pi ft)]+offset by variable projection
withheld: Physical tap recordings
Intrinsic material damping
Global identification of arbitrary audio from a local fit
reviews.incomingEvidence: S1B exposed drive-chain instability; a free-decay rate can cancel constant gain but receiver dynamics and multiple modes remain unresolved.
reviews.nextDecision: S2B: test mode overlap, noise and exact exponential-gain/decay ambiguity using the same frozen importer.

independentChecks.proof: With a 16-sample period y[n+16]=exp(-4*16/8000)y[n]; constant gain and phase cancel in the ratio, whereas time-varying gain need not.

reviews.title: A good decay fit can still describe recording gain
reviews.question: Which model failures can residuals and window changes detect, and which remain exactly ambiguous?
reviews.finding: The fixture detects overlapping modes through large residuals, but exponential gain and a different decay generate byte-identical recordings; a low residual cannot resolve that ambiguity.
reviews.scope: Base=.2 exp(-4t)cos(2pi500t); overlap adds .06exp(-1.5t)cos(2pi512t); gain-drift multiplies base by exp(2t); alternate physical decay is .2exp(-2t)cos(2pi500t)
withheld: Every bad recording is caught by the 5% fixture flag
Intrinsic damping identified from an uncalibrated record
Exponential gain as a universal phone-AGC model
reviews.incomingEvidence: S2A gained amplitude/phase robustness only under a single-mode, fixed-gain model. S1B already showed shared-chain assumptions can fail.
reviews.nextDecision: S3A: add spatial complex observations; distinguish magnitude-only ambiguity from known-basis coefficient recovery.

independentChecks.proof: For all real t, exp(2t)*[.2 exp(-4t) cos(1000pi t)]=.2 exp(-2t)cos(1000pi t). Identical samples force identical outcomes for every deterministic recording-only estimator.

reviews.title: Preserve the original recording during analysis
reviews.question: Can a versioned importer preserve source evidence while giving equivalent WAV and CSV analysis?
reviews.finding: A versioned intake preserves raw files and existing outputs, rejects invalid CSV channels and source/symlink collisions, and gives identical decoded WAV/CSV traces.
reviews.scope: Protected filesystem admission around the frozen S2A single-mode fitter; this is software/metrology verification, not new physics
withheld: Source authenticity from a hash
Acoustic calibration from file integrity
Safety of using the old frozen CLI as a current entry point
reviews.incomingEvidence: Root review identified historical CLI raw-CSV overwrite risk and ignored CSV channel argument. Advisor replaced the unexecuted geometry candidate with this practical defect repair.
reviews.nextDecision: S3B: test timebase metadata and clock-scale ambiguity using identical PCM samples with declared versus corrected times.

independentChecks.scope: Integrity and channel admission of declared files; neither source authenticity nor physical calibration.

reviews.title: The time axis is a calibration premise
reviews.question: Can identical samples yield different absolute decay and frequency under different clock labels?
reviews.finding: Identical samples give proportionally different absolute frequency and decay under a changed timebase; an independently known reference conditionally fixes the scale. The repaired timestamp test now exercises timestamp validation.
withheld: Actual phone-clock calibration
A same-clock tone as an independent reference
Low residual as proof of correct physical time
An untested nonuniform-time control from the preserved first attempt
reviews.incomingEvidence: S3A preserved sample bytes but treats header/timestamp timing as input. S2B established low residuals cannot certify physical interpretation.
reviews.nextDecision: S4A: test what an additional phase-referenced spatial observation can identify in a declared 1D wave model.

independentChecks.proof: Samples depend only on alpha/Fs_actual and f/Fs_actual. Scaling (alpha,f,Fs_actual) together leaves every sample unchanged. A timebase or independent frequency reference fixes this scale only by adding a premise.

reviews.title: A spatial magnitude map loses phase and direction
reviews.question: What changes when a magnitude map is replaced by independent phase-referenced spatial samples?
reviews.finding: Dense magnitude observations retain exact global-phase and conjugate-swap ambiguities; two quarter-wave-spaced complex samples recover coefficients only in the declared known-basis, shared-phase model.
reviews.scope: p(x)=A exp(-ikx)+B exp(ikx); k=2pi f/c; partner coefficients(B*,A*) give conjugate p; global phase multiplies p without changing magnitude
withheld: Unique material or source identity
A conjugate partner satisfying an independently fixed incident-direction/passivity constraint
Automatic phase reference across sequential phone recordings
reviews.incomingEvidence: S2B/S3B scalar fits required gain/timebase premises. This loop adds an independent spatial/phase observable instead of another scalar fit.
reviews.nextDecision: S4B: test spatial inverse conditioning, explicit singular kernels and an independently held-out phase observation.

independentChecks.proof: Conjugate-swapping A,B conjugates p(x), preserving |p| for all x. Multiplying both by exp(i phi) also preserves |p|. At quarter wavelength, the explicit inverse recovers complex coefficients only with the assumed basis and phase reference.

reviews.title: Spacing and a withheld position test the spatial inverse
reviews.question: When does a second spatial sample add stable information, and can a withheld sample expose phase drift?
reviews.finding: Spatial inverse conditioning depends on separation; a two-point exact fit can hide channel phase drift while an independent withheld point exposes this declared mismatch.
reviews.scope: M(x)=[exp(-ikx),exp(ikx)]; singular values sqrt(2±2|cos(kDelta)|); norm-bounded noise eta U_min gives coefficient error eta/sigma_min
withheld: Phase calibration of an ordinary phone
A third channel certifying every model assumption
Worst-case noise as an empirical microphone distribution
reviews.incomingEvidence: S4A ideal quarter-wave inversion succeeded, but actual positions/phase/noise determine whether its extra channel is informative.
reviews.nextDecision: S5A: choose a feasible scalar sound bench with interleaved support/reference observations; test finite-order drift cancellation before a complete recorded-file dry run.

independentChecks.proof: Gram eigenvalues are 2 +/- 2|cos(theta)|. At the withheld eighth wavelength, p_h=(p_0+p_quarter)/sqrt(2); a drift delta only at the second point causes heldout error |delta|/sqrt(2) and least-squares residual |delta|/2.

reviews.title: Counterbalance the household comparison before recording
reviews.question: Does a balanced trial order remove a declared recording drift, and which condition-linked rival remains?
reviews.finding: Balanced ABBA/BAAB order cancels the declared linear acquisition drift in positive and zero-effect generated tap fixtures; it does not distinguish an exactly equivalent condition-linked gain rival.
reviews.scope: alpha_recorded=4+Delta*B-.08*j; amplitude g exp(-alpha_recorded*t)cos(2pi500t); rival intrinsicDelta0 plus condition-linked gain exp(-2B*t) has identical samples toDelta2
withheld: A physical spoon measurement
Intrinsic material change from the fitted contrast
Protection against arbitrary drift or condition-linked nuisance
Public demo labels providing blinding
reviews.incomingEvidence: S4B complex inversion needed phase hardware absent from an ordinary-phone bench. Final round prioritizes a preregistered spoon-support comparison and reproducible data intake.
reviews.nextDecision: S5B: validate the complete manifest-driven recording dry run, retaining excluded trials and withholding the primary contrast when the planned comparison is incomplete.

independentChecks.proof: The contrast equals Delta - .08*(mean order_B-mean order_A): gaps8 and0 yield blocked bias-.64 and balanced zero. Multiplying a Delta=0 signal by exp(-2*B*t) gives the Delta=2 signal identically, so order balance cannot remove that condition-linked rival.

reviews.title: Run the full plan and report every exclusion
reviews.question: Can a strict batch workflow preserve evidence, align impacts, and withhold a primary result for an incomplete plan?
reviews.finding: The complete generated-file plan yields its declared recorded-channel contrast; impact alignment is exercised, raw files are preserved, and incomplete or malformed plans cannot produce a primary result.
reviews.scope: Frozen trial IDs/order/condition, required declared acquisition metadata, SHA-256 admission, impact-relative single-mode fits through unchanged intake_v2; only all planned eligible trials produce primary contrast
withheld: A physical bench study
Metadata or hashes authenticating acoustic calibration
An incomplete survivor contrast substituted for the locked primary
Sound effects implying consciousness or a metaphysical source
reviews.incomingEvidence: S5A balanced order corrected only declared order drift. The final workflow must preserve every raw trial and avoid silently replacing incomplete preregistered results with selected survivors.
reviews.nextDecision: B1: after the completed sound program, freeze exact reporter/prior/leak joint distributions and test apparent independent corroboration.

reviews.title: Agreement is not additional information
reviews.question: Can target-prior imbalance and common reporters mimic corroboration, and does a second report add target information?
reviews.finding: Prior-biased agreeing reporters can contain zero target information; copied reports add no conditional information, while independent informative reports do. An identically specified receiver and ordinary leak remain observationally equivalent.
reviews.scope: Exact P(T,A,B), T,A,B in {0,1,2,3}. L(r|t)=lambda*1[r=t]+(1-lambda)/4. The conditional receiver map with kappa=lambda equals the ordinary leak map by construction.
withheld: Measured AI or human behavior
AI consciousness predicting concealed-target knowledge
A positive score identifying a higher source
IID binomial calibration for a study-level shared latent or a balanced-block target design
reviews.incomingEvidence: S5A condition-linked gain and S5B metadata show that matching observations and declared labels do not identify mechanism or custody. B1 examines the analogous prior/common-reporter/leak ambiguity. Original R6 covered uniform target hits and optional stopping, not this joint-information map.
reviews.nextDecision: B2: freeze a finite balanced randomization and scoring family; compare prespecified, post-selected and max-calibrated scores with an untouched holdout.

independentChecks.proof: Integer weights over6400 exactly determine the single-trial joint law. B=A makes conditional added information zero; informative conditionally independent reports add information. Relabeling the identical copied-leak distribution as a receiver does not identify its cause. Binomial tails assume independent repeated trials.

reviews.title: Freeze the correspondence before the holdout
reviews.question: How much apparent correspondence arises from selecting among four correlated semantic scoring rules, and does that selection survive an independent balanced holdout?
reviews.finding: Choosing the best cyclic scoring rule raises the discovery score and its achieved rejection rate relative to a fixed rule; an independent holdout returns to mean8. In this discrete fixture, naive-selected and max-calibrated rejection rates coincide below nominal5%.
reviews.scope: Exact uniform distribution over 2520 permutations of balanced target labels. Four cyclic scoring matrices use 2 for an exact shifted label, 1 for either adjacent cyclic label, 0 for the opposite. Reports are fixed. The best discovery mapping is frozen before a fresh independent holdout.
withheld: An empirical semantic or synchronicity effect
Nominal-alpha exceedance in this particular fixture
A known-map positive control establishing a higher source
Unrestricted retrospective interpretation identifying a mechanism
reviews.incomingEvidence: B1 demonstrated prior and common-reporter ambiguity despite high scores. Balancing targets removes that particular advantage; B2 tests remaining flexibility in how correspondence is scored. The Pauli event-window example motivates fixed scoring/window boundaries but supplies no statistical evidence for this model.
reviews.nextDecision: B3: freeze crossed state/prompt interventions with scripted report and evaluator-cue channels; test functional state access without phenomenal ground-truth labels.

independentChecks.proof: The independent balanced holdout has the same fixed-rule distribution for every selected cyclic shift. Thus discovery selection changes the maximum distribution but not the untouched holdout mean. At alpha=.05 discreteness makes naive-selected and max-calibrated decisions coincide; neither exceeds nominal .05 in this fixture.

reviews.title: Intervene on state, prompt and evaluator separately
reviews.question: When self-reports match observationally, which crossed interventions distinguish functional state access from prompt following, and which judgments remain evaluator effects?
reviews.finding: Crossed state/prompt observations distinguish the two stipulated functional mechanisms that coincide observationally; scripted affirmation and evaluator effects remain separate from state-access accuracy.
reviews.scope: Exact binary factorial channels Z,P,R,F,E,V. Observational P=Z; crossed P and Z independent. One scripted R channel reads Z and another reads P, both with .9 accuracy to their input. F follows prompt framing; E independently cues a scripted evaluator V. No variable represents phenomenal consciousness.
withheld: Actual AI or human introspection results
Phenomenal-consciousness labels or probabilities
Measured evaluator bias
A functional state-readout identifying a higher consciousness source
reviews.incomingEvidence: B2 showed that selecting an interpretation on discovery does not establish a held-out relationship. B3 freezes the report/evaluator map and uses crossed interventions to distinguish a known functional causal mechanism from matched observational reports.
reviews.nextDecision: STOP after B3: all13 authorized computational reviews are complete; no further research round selected. Physical and live-AI follow-ups remain proposals.

independentChecks.proof: When P=Z the two report channels coincide on all observed cells. Crossed independent P,Z exposes their off-diagonal difference. Summing the stipulated evaluator channel changes V by1/4 under E while the R marginal is unchanged. These are functional channel identities, without a phenomenal-consciousness variable or observed AI/human judgments.
